readings.title: Job's Reply to Bildad
readings.subtitle: The Impossibility of Contending with the Creator
readings.text:
[Job 9:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said,
[2] “Truly I know it is so. But how is man right with <dn>Elohim</dn>?
[3] If one wished to dispute with <dn>Him</dn>, he would not answer <dn>Him</dn> one time out of a thousand.
[4] Wise in heart and potent of power – who has hardened himself against <dn>Him</dn> and is at peace?
[5] <dn>He</dn> who removes mountains, and they do not know it, when <dn>He</dn> overturns them in <dn>His</dn> displeasure;
[6] who shakes the earth out of its place, and its columns tremble;
[7] who commands the sun, and it does not rise; and <dn>He</dn> seals up the stars,
[8] stretching out the heavens by <dn>Himself</dn>, and treading upon the waves of the sea;
[9] who made Ash, Kesil, and Kimah, and the rooms of the south;
[10] who performs great and unsearchable deeds, and innumerable wonders.
[11] Look, <dn>He</dn> goes by me, and I do not see; and <dn>He</dn> moves past, but I do not discern <dn>Him</dn>.
[12] Look, <dn>He</dn> snatches away, who brings it back? Who says to <dn>Him</dn>, ‘What are <dn>You</dn> doing?’
[13] <dn>Eloah</dn> does not turn back <dn>His</dn> displeasure, the helpers of pride stoop under <dn>Him</dn>.
[14] How much less would I answer <dn>Him</dn>, choose my words with <dn>Him</dn>?
[15] For though I were righteous, I would not answer <dn>Him</dn>. I pray to <dn>Him</dn> for my right-ruling.
[16] Though I had called and <dn>He</dn> answered me, I would not believe that <dn>He</dn> was listening to my voice.
[17] For <dn>He</dn> crushes me with a storm, and has multiplied my wounds for no cause.
[18] <dn>He</dn> does not allow me to recover my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
[19] If I speak of power? Look, <dn>He</dn> is potent. And if of right-ruling? Who sets me a time?
[20] If I am righteous? My mouth would declare me wrong. Am I perfect? It would declare me perverse.
[21] Am I perfect? Do I not know my own being? I despise my life!
[22] It is all the same, therefore I say, ‘<dn>He</dn> destroys the perfect and the wrong.’
[23] If the scourge slays suddenly, <dn>He</dn> laughs at the trial of the innocent.
[24] Earth has been given into the hand of the wrong. <dn>He</dn> covers the faces of its judges. If it is not <dn>He</dn>, then who is it?
[25] My days have become swifter than a runner – they have fled, they have not seen good.
[26] They have passed by like swift ships, like an eagle swooping on its prey.
[27] If I say, ‘Let me forget my complaint, let me put off my sad face, and let me smile,’
[28] I shall be afraid of all my sufferings. I know that <dn>You</dn> do not hold me innocent.
[29] If I am wrong, why should I labour in vain?
[30] If I washed myself with snow water, and cleansed my hands with soap,
[31] then <dn>You</dn> would plunge me into a ditch, and my garments shall abhor me.
[32] For <dn>He</dn> is not a man as I am that I answer <dn>Him</dn>, and we come together into right-ruling.
[33] There is no mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
[34] Let <dn>Him</dn> take <dn>His</dn> rod away from me, and let not <dn>His</dn> dread frighten me.
[35] Then I would speak and not fear <dn>Him</dn>, for I am not so within myself.

readings.title: Job's Plea to the Almighty
readings.subtitle: A Cry from the Depths of Suffering
readings.text:
[Job 10:1] “My being has grown weary of life. I let loose my complaint, I speak in the bitterness of my being.
[2] I say to <dn>Eloah</dn>, ‘Do not declare me wrong, show me why <dn>You</dn> strive with me.
[3] Is it good to <dn>You</dn> that <dn>You</dn> should crush, that <dn>You</dn> should despise the work of <dn>Your</dn> hands, and shine on the counsel of the wrong?
[4] Do <dn>You</dn> have eyes of flesh? Do <dn>You</dn> see as man sees?
[5] Are <dn>Your</dn> days like the days of a mortal man? Are <dn>Your</dn> years like the days of a mighty man,
[6] that <dn>You</dn> should seek for my crookedness and search out my sin?
[7] For <dn>You</dn> know that I am not wrong, and there is no one to deliver from <dn>Your</dn> hand.
[8] <dn>Your</dn> hands have made me and shaped me, together all around, yet <dn>You</dn> destroy me.
[9] Remember, please, that <dn>You</dn> have made me like clay. And would <dn>You</dn> turn me into dust again?
[10] Did <dn>You</dn> not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
[11] Skin and flesh <dn>You</dn> put on me, and wove me with bones and sinews.
[12] Life and loving-commitment <dn>You</dn> have bestowed on me, and <dn>Your</dn> visitation has preserved my spirit.
[13] And these <dn>You</dn> have laid up in <dn>Your</dn> heart, I know that this was with <dn>You</dn>:
[14] If I sin, then <dn>You</dn> watch me, and let no crookedness of mine go unpunished.
[15] If I am wrong, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I would not lift up my head – filled with shame and seeing my grief!
[16] If I lift it up high, <dn>You</dn> hunt me as a lion, and again <dn>You</dn> would show <dn>Yourself</dn> marvellous against me.
[17] <dn>You</dn> renew <dn>Your</dn> witnesses against me, and increase <dn>Your</dn> vexation toward me; changes and a host are with me.
[18] So why have <dn>You</dn> brought me forth from the womb? Oh, that I had perished and no eye had seen me!
[19] I should have been as though I had not been – brought from the womb to the burial-site.
[20] Are not my days few? Then cease! Leave me alone, so that I brighten up a little,
[21] Before I go, and not return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death,
[22] a land as dark as darkness itself, as the shadow of death, without any order, whose light is as darkness.”

readings.title: Zophar's First Speech
readings.subtitle: The Accusation of Hidden Iniquity
readings.text:
[Job 11:1] And Tsophar the Na‛amathite answered and said,
[2] “Should a multitude of words go unanswered? And should a man of lips be declared right?
[3] Should your babblings silence men? And should you mock, and no one make you ashamed?
[4] Since you have said, ‘My discourse is flawless, and I have been clean in <dn>Your</dn> eyes.’
[5] But if only <dn>Eloah</dn> would speak, and open <dn>His</dn> lips against you,
[6] and show you the secrets of wisdom, doubling your ability. Know then that <dn>Eloah</dn> forgets some of your crookedness for you.
[7] Would you find out <dn>Eloah</dn> by searching, or search out the end of the <dn>Almighty</dn>?
[8] It is higher than the heavens – what would you do? Deeper than She’ol – what would you know?
[9] Their measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
[10] If <dn>He</dn> passes through and shuts up, and gathers, then who does reverse it?
[11] For <dn>He</dn> knows false men. When <dn>He</dn> sees wickedness does <dn>He</dn> not consider it?
[12] But a senseless man takes heart when a wild donkey’s colt is born a man!
[13] If you would prepare your heart, and stretch out your hands toward <dn>Him</dn>;
[14] if wickedness were in your hand, put it far away and do not let perverseness dwell in your tents;
[15] then indeed you shall lift up your face without spot; and you shall stand firm, and not be afraid,
[16] because you would forget sorrow, and remember it as waters that have passed away,
[17] and your life would be brighter than noon. You would soar upward, you would be like the morning.
[18] And you shall trust, because there is expectancy. And when you have searched you shall lie down in safety.
[19] And you shall rest, and no one would make you afraid, and many shall seek your favour.
[20] But the eyes of the wrong are consumed, and they shall not escape, and their expectancy is the breathing out of life!”

readings.title: Job's Reply to Zophar
readings.subtitle: The Unsearchable Wisdom and Power of YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[Job 12:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said,
[2] “Truly you are the people, and wisdom would die with you!
[3] But I, like you, have a heart too; I am not less than you. And who does not know such as these?
[4] I have become a laughing-stock to my friends – one who has called on <dn>Eloah</dn> and <dn>He</dn> answered him! A laughing-stock is the righteous, the perfect one!
[5] A lamp is despised in the thought of one who is at ease – prepared for those whose feet slip.
[6] The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke <dn>Ěl</dn> are complacent, to him who brings <dn>Eloah</dn> into his hand!
[7] But now ask the beasts, and they teach you; and the birds of the heavens, and they declare it to you;
[8] or speak to the earth, and it teaches you; and the fish of the sea inform you.
[9] Who among all these does not know that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done this,
[10] in whose hand is the life of all that live, and the breath of all mankind?
[11] Does the ear not try words? And the mouth taste food for itself?
[12] With the aged is wisdom, and understanding with length of days.
[13] With <dn>Him</dn> are wisdom and might, <dn>He</dn> has counsel and understanding.
[14] Look, <dn>He</dn> breaks down, and it is not rebuilt. If <dn>He</dn> imprisons a man, there is no release.
[15] Look, <dn>He</dn> withholds the waters, and they dry up. And <dn>He</dn> sends them out, and they overwhelm the earth.
[16] With <dn>Him</dn> are strength and ability. The misled and the misleader are <dn>His</dn>.
[17] <dn>He</dn> leads counsellors away stripped, and makes judges go mad.
[18] <dn>He</dn> loosens the bonds of sovereigns, and binds a girdle on their loins;
[19] who leads away priests as a spoil, and overthrows the mighty;
[20] turning aside the lip of the trusted ones, and takes away the discernment of the elders;
[21] pouring scorn on nobles, and loosens the girdle of the strong;
[22] revealing deep matters out of darkness, and <dn>He</dn> brings the shadow of death to light;
[23] making nations great, and <dn>He</dn> destroys them; spreading out the nations, and <dn>He</dn> leads them out.
[24] turning aside the heart of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and <dn>He</dn> makes them wander in a pathless waste.
[25] They grope in darkness, having no light, and <dn>He</dn> makes them stagger like a drunkard.
